guide_zh.overview: AIHawk: AI job application bot, automated job search, job hunting, auto-apply to resume-matching jobs while you sleep.

readme.markdown:
An AI job application bot: automated job search, then it auto-applies to the jobs that match your resume, while you sleep.

FEATURED IN
Business Insider · TechCrunch · Semafor · Wired · The Verge · Vanity Fair · 404 Media
--- ## How it works Give it your resume. The job search finds the postings that fit, you pick, and it fills in and sends each job application on the company's own form. | Step | What happens | |---|---| | **1. Reads your resume** | Turns it into a search: the titles, the skills and the places that fit you. | | **2. Searches** | 6 million postings of the last 60 days from 37 public sources, rebuilt every five hours, searched on your computer. | | **3. Scores** | Asks of every posting, against your resume, one question: is it in line with you? How sure the answer is makes the score, from 1 to 5. 50 jobs to a page, the next one ready while you read this one. | | **4. You pick** | Select the jobs you want and say yes once. | | **5. Applies** | A real Firefox opens the company's form, fills every required field, attaches your CV and sends. | | **6. Keeps the answer** | What each page said, with a screenshot, for every application. | --- ## Install Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/feder-cr/Jobs_Applier_AI_Agent/main/run.ps1 | iex ``` Linux: ```bash curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/feder-cr/Jobs_Applier_AI_Agent/main/run.sh | sh ``` You need a key: [get one from OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai/ref/ref_accd17afb78fc95ac4d7). The first start downloads about 250 MB and takes a minute or two; after that it opens in seconds, also without a connection. Nothing else needs installing first (on Linux, `curl`). The first application brings the browser, about 430 MB more, and opens it in a window: on Linux that needs a desktop. ## The count AIHawk tells us how it is used, so we know what to fix. It sends these events to [PostHog](https://posthog.com), with a random id made on your computer the first time, so each computer counts once: | Event | When | What it carries | |---|---|---| | `app_started` | AIHawk opens | AIHawk's version, the operating system | | `start_step` | each step of a start | the step (key asked or saved, resume read or not, mail, jobs downloading, the first job on the screen, jobs ready), the seconds since AIHawk opened, and where it applies the kind of file the resume is (pdf, docx…), how many parts of the jobs had come, or the kind of error that stopped the start | | `search` | a search ends | how many jobs it found, and how many of them were new | | `jobs_scored` | Jev reads a round | how many postings, how many it answered for, how long it took, the model | | `app_closed` | AIHawk closes | the last step it reached, whether it searched, how long it was open | | `application` | an application ends | how it went (sent, sent but not confirmed, refused, blocked, failed), why in one word (captcha, login, closed posting…), whether a plugin was used, the kind of site (a plugin's name, or the vendor's name when the form is on a known application site such as Workday or Greenhouse, else "other": never the address), the models, the gateway, the steps, the time, and the tokens each model read and wrote | Nothing about you or the jobs goes with them: no name, email, resume, answer, company or link. The number on the badge above is the applications sent. The count is always on; a dry run is not counted. --- [Sites](docs/sites.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) · [Writing a plugin](docs/plugins.md) · [Wiki](https://github.com/feder-cr/Jobs_Applier_AI_Agent/wiki) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Security](SECURITY.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
